options.text: A React framework that adds routing, rendering, and data fetching on top of React
A replacement for React that uses a different component model
A CSS framework for styling React apps
A database used by React applications

questions.explanation: Next.js is a framework built on top of React. It keeps React's components and hooks and adds routing, rendering strategies, data fetching, and an optimized build.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the App Router are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Files and folders inside app/ define the application's URLs
Components are Server Components by default
It uses getServerSideProps to fetch data
It is the recommended approach for new Next.js projects

questions.explanation: In the App Router, the file system defines routes, components render on the server by default, and it is recommended for new projects. getServerSideProps belongs to the older Pages Router.

questions.prompt: In the App Router, which special directory holds your routes? Type just the folder name.
questions.explanation: The App Router uses the app/ directory: a page.tsx inside a folder becomes that folder's route.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.

pairs.right: Runs on the server by default in the App Router
Runs in the browser; opted into with "use client"
The app/ directory system for new projects

questions.explanation: The App Router (app/) renders Server Components by default; Client Components opt into the browser with "use client". The Pages Router (pages/) is the older system.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a first request to a Server Component page in order.

items.text: A browser requests a URL like /about
Next.js runs the matching page.tsx on the server
The component is turned into HTML
The finished HTML is sent to the browser and displayed

questions.explanation: A Server Component runs on the server in response to the request, is rendered to HTML, and that HTML is sent to the browser — giving fast first paint and good SEO.
